why: exact title — the baseline. If this is not rank 1, nothing else matters.
exact title of a SIBLING by the same author; must not lose to 'עולם טבעת'.
series disambiguation, the hardest ranking case: five titles share 'הצי האבוד' and only the last word separates them.
the series prefix alone — all five volumes, none missing.
stored title carries the definite article ('הנופלים'), the user does not. Handled by substring, no variant needed.
the OTHER direction: the user adds a definite article the catalogue does not have ('כוכב ניוטרון'). This is the case particle-stripping exists for.
both words carry a particle in the stored title ('הצעקה האדומה'); substring covers both.
final letter ם, folded by normalize() so it is the same token as a medial מ.
one distinctive word out of the middle of a title.
author typed WITHOUT the geresh; stored as באלדאצ'י. normalize() deletes it in-word on both sides.
the same work is stored three times with three punctuation styles — geresh, backtick, and an ampersand. All three must come back from one query.

RANKING, not filtering: three books match ('מהעיר הדוממת', 'עיר', 'עיר הזמן') and the exact title must win. Alphabetical order puts 'מהעיר הדוממת' first, so this query fails without a relevance score.
RANKING, title over author: one book has it in the TITLE ('מלך ירושלים'), another has it in the AUTHOR's name. Alphabetical order puts the author match first.
an exact title that is also a prefix of a longer one ('...מודרנית'); the shorter, exact answer wins.
mixed script — the stored title ends in a Latin numeral 'III'.
author search: every book by them, and nothing else.
author plus a title word — the query shape a person actually types when they half-remember a book.
truncated word: search is substring, so a partial name still finds its books.
two very common words as a whole title — the exact title must beat every book that merely contains one of them.
plain two-word title, no particles, no tricks. The control case.
a numeric title. Short, and would be noise as an infix — must still resolve.
punctuation inside the title; normalize() drops the hyphen on both sides.
no such book. Must return nothing rather than a best guess.
empty search box. Must return nothing, NOT the whole library.
